source_text: Fragmenta varia 88 Τὸ μὴ μόνον ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ καὶ Θεόν, καθὼς καὶ Ἱερεμίας ὁ προφήτης λέγει· οὗτος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, οὐ λογισθήσεται ἕτερος πρὸς αὐτόν. Ἐξεῦρε πᾶσαν ὁδὸν ἐπιστήμης καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν Ἰακὼβ τῶι παιδὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἰσραὴλ τῶι ἠγαπημένωι ὑπ' αὐτοῦ. Μετὰ ταῦτα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὤφθη καὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις συνανεστράφη. Πότε δὲ συνανεστράφη ἀνθρώποις, εἰ μὴ ὅτε συνεγεννήθη μετ' αὐτῶν ἐκ παρθένου καὶ συνενηπίασε καὶ συνηυξήθη καὶ συνέφαγε καὶ συνέπιε καὶ τὰ ἄλλα; 90 Εἰ γὰρ τὰς εὐχὰς ποιεῖσθαι δεῖ, φησίν, ὑπὲρ τῆς καθολικῆς Ἐκκλησίας τῆς ἀπὸ περάτων τῆς οἰκουμένης, πολλῷ μᾶλλον καὶ τὴν πρόνοιαν ὑπὲρ ἁπάσης αὐτῆς ἐπιδείκνυσθαι δεῖ καὶ ὁμοίως ἁπασῶν κήδεσθαι καὶ μεριμνᾶν πάσας.
thought_title: The one who appeared is God, and the whole Church deserves equal care
orientation: Eustathius opens by arguing from Jeremiah that the one who appeared on earth and lived among humans is not only human but also God, then turns to the duty of providential care for the whole catholic Church.
pass_a_gloss: That he is not only human, but also God, as also the prophet says: this is our God, no other will be reckoned beside him. He found out the whole way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob his child and to Israel the one beloved by him. After these things he was seen on the earth and lived among humans. And when did he live among humans, if not when he was born together with them from a virgin and shared infancy and grew up together with them and ate and drank with them and all the other things? For if prayers must be made, Scripture says, for the catholic Church which is from the ends of the world, much more must providence be shown for all of it and care and concern for all its parts equally.

choices.english: no other will be reckoned beside him
choices.why: Keeps the future passive force of λογισθήσεται and the comparative sense of πρὸς αὐτόν as 'beside him' rather than 'compared to him', preserving the exclusivity claim.
rejected: no other will be counted with him
no other shall be compared to him

choices.english: He found out the whole way of knowledge
choices.why: Ἐξεῦρε is aorist of ἐξευρίσκω, 'found out' or 'discovered'; πᾶσαν ὁδὸν is 'the whole way', not 'every way', keeping the singular path sense.
rejected: He discovered every path of knowledge
He found all the way of knowledge

choices.why: παῖς can mean child or servant; the brief identifies Jacob as 'his child (τῶι παιδὶ αὐτοῦ = his child/servant)', and 'child' preserves the relational intimacy with the following 'beloved'.

choices.english: was born together with them from a virgin
choices.why: The compound συν- in συνεγεννήθη means 'together with', and μετ' αὐτῶν makes the shared birth explicit; 'from a virgin' keeps ἐκ παρθένου as the source of birth.
rejected: was born with them of a virgin
was begotten together with them from a virgin

choices.why: The verb συννηπιάζω is a hapax compound meaning to be an infant together with; 'shared infancy' captures the joint experience without inventing a smoother English verb.

choices.english: which is from the ends of the world
choices.why: ἀπὸ περάτων means 'from the ends', and τῆς οἰκουμένης is the inhabited world per the glossary; the relative clause keeps the spatial extent of the Church.
rejected: from the ends of the inhabited world

bible_refs.note: οὗτος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, οὐ λογισθήσεται ἕτερος πρὸς αὐτόν. Ἐξεῦρε πᾶσαν ὁδὸν ἐπιστήμης καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν Ἰακὼβ τῶι παιδὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἰσραὴλ τῶι ἠγαπημένωι ὑπ' αὐτοῦ. Μετὰ ταῦτα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὤφθη καὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις συνανεστράφη.

pass_b_english: The one who appeared on earth and lived among human beings was not only human but also God, as Jeremiah the prophet says: “This is our God; no other will be reckoned beside him. He found out the whole way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob his child and to Israel, whom he loved. After this he was seen on earth and lived among human beings” (Baruch 3:36-38, attributed to Jeremiah). When did he live among human beings, if not when he was born together with them from a virgin, shared infancy, grew up together with them, ate and drank with them, and shared all the rest of human life?

For if prayers must be made, Scripture says, for the catholic Church that is from the ends of the world, then all the more must providence be shown for the whole of it, and care and concern for all its parts equally.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes English as 'human', banned includes 'human person', 'man', 'mankind'. English uses 'human beings' which is not the fixed term 'human'. This violates glossary.
last_rejected.ruling: ἄνθρωπος naturally renders as 'human beings' in plural context; glossary 'human' covers this range, not a violation.

last_rejected.why: The 'he says' in 'For if prayers must be made, he says' is ambiguous—does it refer to Eustathius or Jeremiah? In source, φησίν follows the Jeremiah quotation and introduces a new argument by Eustathius. The English 'he says' could mislead readers into thinking Jeremiah is still speaking, but contextually it's likely Eustathius. The brief marks Jeremiah as speaker for sections frag-open, frag-rem-early, frag-rem-mid. This suggests 'he says' should attach to Jeremiah, but the content (prayers for catholic Church) is Eustathius's argument, not Jeremiah's quotation. The English 'he says' with lowercase after quotation mark and new paragraph is confusing but may intend Eustathius.
last_rejected.ruling: φησίν is standard citation formula; context after Jeremiah quote makes Eustathius clear, no real ambiguity.

last_rejected.quote: and shared the rest of human life
last_rejected.why: The source has 'and the other things' or 'and the rest'—English adds 'of human life' which is interpretive but within reasonable expansion. Not a strict omission.
last_rejected.ruling: τὰ ἄλλα 'the rest' contextually means rest of human life; interpretive expansion is within normal range.
